text:
anya: quick triage — we need to lock the GA acceptance criteria by EOD. main question: do we push full autoscale + advanced batching now or ship with basic capacity + observability and cut batching for later?

mike: +1 to narrow. batching still flaky across models, could be a regression risk. we can ship with single-tenant autoscale and a knob for later. :thumbsup:

carla: docs/console side needs a couple of pages: SLA summary, model fallbacks, and how to configure autoscale policies. can take docs ownership if we keep the scope minimal.

ben: what does "SLA summary" look like numerically? finance wants a guardrail for pricing before GA. also need a default billing floor for Dedicated.

anya: good call. proposed minimum GA acceptance items: 
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for hosted API for committed plans (documented SLO + measurement)
- Latency: p50/p95 targets per model class (we'll publish targets, not SLAs)
- Observability: per-route traces, token-level cost breakdown in Console
- Docs: onboarding + ops runbook + config examples
- Support: basic oncall coverage + SLA escalation path
- Pricing: visible default tiers + disclaimer for pilot pricing until formal contract

mike: can we write the SLA blurb now? something short we can drop into docs.

carla: here's a draft snippet I can refine — feel free to copy: ```
SLA (GA): Redwood Hosted API will aim to provide 99.9% availability for committed plan customers. Availability is measured as successful responses to health-checked endpoints over a 30-day window. Non-binding latency targets (p50/p95) will be published per-model. Detailed measurement and exceptions in the SLA doc.
```

ben: that helps. finance wants a fallback: if unit cost > expected by >20% for 3 consecutive days, auto-notify finops + rollout temporary quota limits. is that doable?

mike: yes we have a webhook and alert that can do that. I'll add a monitoring rule to the playbook.

ops-bot: Reminder: Oncall rotation for GA must be added to the playbook. Link: https://confluence.example/ga-oncall-playbook

anya: decision so far: scope will be "MVP launch" = hosted API + basic autoscale + observability + docs/runbook. deferring advanced batching and multi-model pipelining to post-GA. owners: carla (docs), mike (monitoring/runbook), ben (pricing guardrails).

carla: I'll drop a PR with the docs outline by noon, then we can iterate.

ben: finance will sign off on default tiers if we include the >20% cost-notify clause and a pilot pricing disclaimer.

mike: I'll add the monitoring rule and the outage-contact list. quick config snippet I'll push to infra channel: ```
monitoring_rule:
  name: pricing-spike
  condition: unit_cost > expected * 1.2 for 72h
  actions: [notify: #finops, limit: reduce-chaos-burst]
```

anya: perfect. next actions: carla PR, mike monitoring rule, ben finalize pricing note. we'll reconvene tomorrow 10am PT to sign off. :calendar: 

ops-bot: Note: Thread archived after 7 days of inactivity.
